* Removed public Redis port exposure from the default Docker Compose files and applied the configured Redis password.
* Redis is no longer exposed on the host by the default Compose files. External Redis clients need a separate connection configuration.
* Run database migrations. Keep the existing `CB_SECRET` and `CB_ENCRYPTION_KEY` values so stored credentials can be decrypted.
* Blocked additional ClickHouse functions that can access external services.
* Fixed PostgreSQL table discovery for custom schema

* Run database migrations and complete the cached chart data backfill before reopening the application. Review the backfill report for charts that need attention.
* Reduced database test time and ran verification jobs in parallel.
* v6 uses the original variable names in every environment. For example, replace `CB_DB_NAME_DEV` with `CB_DB_NAME` and `VITE_APP_API_HOST_DEV` with `VITE_APP_API_HOST`. Apply this change to every `_DEV` variable in environment files, Docker settings, hosting secrets, service-mana

- Restricted MongoDB queries to supported read-only operations.
- No new environment variables or database migrations are required.

## Changelog

### ✨ New features

* Introduced a **Dataset Intelligence** model to help the AI orchestrator understand your data format better. All datasets will get an intelligence model attached automatically, but can also be edited manually from the dataset editor screen. This results in AI re-using datasets better and work much faster than before.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

* Fixed regression with fieldSchema remaining stale when the data format would change
* Fixed issue with constructing tabular

## KiviDB v1.2.2
1.2.2 fixes [GHSA-8rm8-p5c5-g3mr](https://github.com/kividbio/kividb/security/advisories/GHSA-8rm8-p5c5-g3mr) (medium): a multi-key write over a key past its TTL could make the whole server stop answering, until a restart, when a search index existed and was being changed at the same time. Any client allowed to run ordinary string and hash writes and one `FT.ALIAS*` command could trigger it; with a vector index and expiring hash fields, background work could too. - A reshard under load no longer loses acknowledged writes, with `MIGRATE` (`redis-cli --cluster reshard`) or with `CLUSTER MIGRATION IMPORT` (the Kubernetes operator): a write checks inside the write gate whether its keys have left the node, and is sent on with `-ASK` or `-MOVED` if they have. The same holds for `EXEC` and scripts, and for every other way a slot leaves a node (#331, #337, #339, #407).
- `MIGRATE` no longer stops `redis-cli --cluster reshard` with `TRYAGAIN` for an unchanged hash whose fiel

- **Replicas stand for election only when they are in step,** as in Redis: one restarted while its master is down no longer takes over (unless `cluster-replica-validity-factor` is 0), and one in the middle of a full sync never does.
- **Memory freed by dropping a large vector index stays with the process.** After `FT.DROPINDEX` and deleting its documents (a million 1536-dimension vectors in [the vector benchmark](https://github.com/kividbio/kividb/blob/v1.2.0/benchmarks/1.2.0/vector/README.md)), `used_memor
